Subject: Post-call: audit export sample & scope — next steps

Hi Liam / Maya — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so everyone has the same view.

Call recap (from Hometown Health requirements):
- You need an evidence export of data-access logs showing who accessed what and when across the product for a defined scope.
- Priority: user-level access events for the last 90 days; sample export for legal/security review.
- Residency requirement: logs must remain in US (us-east-1) for delivery and storage.
- Preferred format: CSV compressed (or parquet if we recommend).

Open clarifying items for your confirmation:
1) Confirm the event fields you need (we suggested user_id (pseudonymized), resource_id, action, timestamp, source_ip, session_id, role). Please add/remove fields.
2) Confirm exact time window you want in the sample (we heard 90 days but will confirm).
3) Residency: is exporting into a temporary S3 link in us-east-1 acceptable, or do you need continuous retention in your environment?

What we will deliver (proposed):
- Sample export (CSV) covering the agreed 30/90-day window, pseudonymized user identifiers, and a README describing export schema and redaction steps.
- A short note on retention and residency options (hosted vs dedicated/private options).
- Links to SOC 2 summary and our audit log schema.

Timeline: target to deliver sample + README by Tue Nov 10 COB PT, provided we confirm fields/time window today.

Attachment: hometown_sample_requirements.pdf (the notes I took on the call)

Thanks — I’ll coordinate once we get your confirmation on the three clarifying items above.

—

Thanks Soojin — good recap. Quick answers below so you can proceed.

1) Fields: please include the following in the sample: user_id (pseudonymized but stable across events), resource_id, action_type, iso_timestamp (UTC), source_ip, session_id, role, request_params (truncated to 200 chars), and whether the event triggered data access (boolean).
2) Time window: 90 days is correct for the initial sample.
3) Residency: we require the exported artifacts to be stored and accessed only in US East (us-east-1) while under review. A temporary presigned S3 link in us-east-1 is fine for the sample. For ongoing retention after review, we’ll discuss via procurement.

Also: Can you provide a short attestation or link to your SOC 2 report and a description of how user identifiers will be pseudonymized? Our legal team will want that with the sample.

Prefer CSV (gzip) for the sample. If parquet is significantly more performant, note that as an option but deliver CSV first.

Thanks — Liam

Liam Carter

Soojin — thanks for the context. Quick status and plan: 

1) Sample export: we can produce a CSV (gzip) with the requested fields and stable pseudonymized user_id. Pseudonymization method: SHA256(user_id + salt) truncated to 16 chars; documented in README. No reversible identifiers will be included.
2) Size & timeframe: we’ll sample ~20k events across the 90-day window to illustrate schema and edge cases. Expecting to upload audit_export_example.csv.gz and README.txt by Tue Nov 10 5:00pm PT.
3) Residency & retention: for customers on our Dedicated or Private deployments we can ensure exports are created and remain in us-east-1 without cross-region replication. For Hosted accounts, our logging pipeline stores backups in multiple regions for redundancy; however, we can create an ad-hoc export job that runs in us-east-1 and place the artifacts in a controlled S3 bucket restricted to us-east-1 for the sample delivery. We will note this in the README and the compliance pack.
4) SOC 2 & attestation: attached is a redacted SOC 2 summary (SOC2-summary.pdf) and a short attestation paragraph we can include with the sample describing scope and controls. If Hometown needs the full SOC 2 report, procurement will need to process an NDA and evidence request.

Attachments planned for delivery: audit_export_example.csv.gz, README.txt, SOC2-summary.pdf

If Karthik can confirm the export job settings and presigned URL policy, I’ll proceed to run the job and share the link to Liam/Maya.

—
